critical_steps: For K equal to the projection onto span{e1}, the one-block controlled fusion energy equals ||K* f||^2 exactly.
The source-defined analysis operator is the projection H -> span{e1}, so its adjoint is the proper inclusion span{e1} -> H and is not surjective.
The lower controlled K-fusion inequality is equivalent to A K K* <= T* T.
Douglas range inclusion converts this domination exactly into R(K) subseteq R(T*).
If K is surjective, the corrected range inclusion reduces to synthesis surjectivity.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional one-block controlled K-fusion frame and Douglas range inclusion theorem.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claims are made about unrelated theorems in the source or about alternative coefficient-space definitions.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects the synthesis-surjectivity characterization in Theorem 10 only.

The corrected range-inclusion criterion presumes the controlled analysis and synthesis operators are well-defined as in the source; the counterexample has a finite-dimensional closed coefficient space, so this issue does not arise there.
A nonindexed erratum or informal author correction may contain the same observation.
title: Surjectivity is too strong for a controlled \(K\)-fusion characterization
